findings.title: A historical tail remains legible
findings.claim: Placed after a city-ending process and beside the pericope's person-bound records, 17:17's counted cohorts leave a historical tail: their sins remain within the Lord's knowledge and sight rather than disappearing into a blank interval.
findings.mechanism: The ordinary guilt sense of ذُنُوبِ remains primary. The root's tail and rear-end image is activated by the focus's generations and post-Noah succession, the earlier carried line, the city's ruin, and the nearby personal records. Khabīr and Baṣīr then make the moral trace legible, while the repeated sufficiency construction links divine knowledge to the prior self-reckoning.
findings.reader_payoff: A generation's disappearance does not make its deeds an unreadable blank; the focus holds historical ruin beside a knowable moral remainder.
findings.containment: The tail is a bounded root image, not a replacement gloss for sin or a literal animal in the historical scene. Temporal after remains temporal, guilt is not inherited, and the focus does not say every cohort followed the same city process.

epistemic.reason: The channel's branches and focus words are supplied, and the pericope provides independent lineage, ruin, and ledger triggers; the tail-to-accountable-residue relation remains analogical.

findings.title: Common provision before divergent ends
findings.claim: After the focus's destruction tally, the next ayat distinguish people pursuing immediate from later outcomes yet say both receive the Lord's gift; read back through the focus's Lord and destruction, this leaves room to understand judgment under provision rather than as simple prior deprivation.
findings.mechanism: The focus's Lord is linked to nurturing and completion. The following routes of hastening and directed pursuit meet the shared extension and granted gift to both groups, explicitly not barred. That provision constrains a simple-withholding reading of the prior destruction, while the ends of the routes remain different.
findings.reader_payoff: Provision and moral outcome are no longer conflated: both groups receive extension, while their pursuits and ends diverge.
findings.containment: The post-focus gift may concern worldly allocation only and may not explain the earlier destroyed generations. This reading does not claim that every cohort received the same provision.

epistemic.reason: The exact 17:18–20 roots return to the focus Lord and destruction carriers, but applying common provision backward to earlier generations is explicitly inferential.

findings.title: Worshippers within the servant address
findings.claim: The added Fātiḥa's first-person confession of worship can make its speakers one possible part of the broad servant class named in 17:17, so the declaration that their sins are known and seen can be heard within prayer as well as historical warning.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier is the possessive phrase His servants. The external 1:5 trigger says we worship You, using the same service root; their contact makes the worshipping speaker an inclusive possible referent of the focus's servant class.
findings.reader_payoff: The historical warning turns back toward the reader's own confession without accusing that reader of a particular sin.
findings.containment: This is an inclusive contextual possibility only. It does not identify every worshipper with the destroyed generations or assert that each reciter has a specified sin.

epistemic.reason: Both surface occurrences are supplied and the shared root is exact; including the reciting community in the broad servant class is an inference, not an identity stated by either ayah.
